answer.rationale: p99 latency spike of 5x target confined to primary region started 90 minutes ago, precisely aligned with a release 2 hours ago. memory_b1 demonstrates that rollback cleared a checkout error spike with no customer impact. Given settlement traffic at peak and heavy write volume, we cannot risk progressive remediation (capacity addition or circuit breakers would only mask the underlying regression). Regional failover would split traffic during peak settlement when consistency matters most. Rolling back to the prior stable build is the fastest path to restore write-path latency while settlement is still active. Verification confirms the precedent of rollback-driven recovery under similar production pressure.
